title: Config-linked output integrity sentinel and signal enrichment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an automated sentinel that directly links structured-output deviations (JSON/schema adherence and per-field quality drop) to recent model and serving configuration changes. The goal is to surface actionable, high-confidence signals when a rollout or config tweak causes a regression in output integrity for typed responses. This ticket focuses on: 1) ingesting config/model diffs and fingerprinting them; 2) enriching standard eval signals with counterfactual reruns and field-level attribution; 3) computing a composite Config-Linked Integrity Score (CLIS) and exposing playbookable alerts and rollback suggestions to console and the rollout system.
acceptance_criteria: CLIS computed and indexed for rollouts covering last 30 days, with per-model and per-config-delta breakdowns
Alerts generated for CLIS > threshold in staging canary and routed to #canary-alerts and console rollouts UI
For flagged regressions, system provides top-3 suspected changes (model version, quantization profile, or batch-config) with an estimated confidence score
Counterfactual rerun job implemented to reproduce signals: ability to rerun a selected sample set against prior pinned baseline and latest config within 30 minutes
Playbook actions surfaced: annotate rollout with suspected cause, pause canary, or create a rollback suggestion with one-click PR link
technical_approach: Change ingestion: consume model/config change events from deployments pipeline and compute compact fingerprints (model_hash, config_hash, quant_profile_id)
Signal enrichment: attach metadata (route, input cohort tags, tokenization profile, sequence_length_bucket) to each eval sample and live trace
Counterfactual reruns: pipeline to re-run a bounded sample set deterministically against previous config to estimate delta (JS divergence per-field, token-level perplexity change)

Attribution scoring: compute per-field delta metrics (schema-violation-rate, missing-fields, extra-fields, type-mismatch), combine with statistical significance and recency into CLIS using a weighted heuristic with tunable weights

Causal heuristics: prioritize changes that co-occur with signal surge (temporal proximity, unique-to-config fingerprint, monotonicity across cohorts), and apply an uncertainty penalty for low-sample cohorts
Storage/indexing: time-series + document store to support fast per-rollout queries and heatmap generation for field-level hotspots
UI surface: add a Rollouts -> Integrity tab showing CLIS trendline, top-affected fields, and suggested suspect changes with confidence
Automation: define safe automation actions (annotate/pause/notify/rollback-suggestion) with manual approval for production rollouts
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (prototype): implement ingestion and offline analysis on 90-day backfill for a single high-volume model and run retrospective to validate signal precision
Phase 1 (internal canaries): enable detection for internal-service rollouts only; wire alerts to #canary-alerts and on-call SRE for triage
Phase 2 (customer opt-in): expose alerting and CLIS in console for customers who opt in, with default conservative thresholds
Phase 3 (auto-suggestions): enable rollback suggestions in console for Dedicated accounts with SLA coverage, gated behind security review
Monitoring and KPIs: iterate thresholds to target <5% false positives during canary phase before broader enablement
monitoring_metrics: CLIS (Config-Linked Integrity Score) — time series per rollout
Counterfactual reproduction success rate — percent of reruns that reproduce signal
False-positive rate measured against manually-investigated incidents
automation_actions: Annotate rollout with suspected change (adds tag & notes to rollout)
Pause canary autoscaling for affected deployment
Create rollback-suggestion PR template with pinned baseline model/config
Open incident in PagerDuty with prefilled context and top-affected sample ids
open_questions: What is the minimal deterministic sample set size per cohort to produce reliable per-field attribution?
Should CLIS be computed per-customer (tenant) or global with cohort breakdowns?
How do we tune thresholds to avoid alert fatigue for low-volume cohorts?
Is counterfactual rerun allowed on private/on-prem customers by default or opt-in only?
What privacy constraints apply to storing input samples for reruns (obfuscation / retention policy)?
